verdict.probe_question: Can OpenFEC data reliably measure where candidate money comes from, at what geographic resolution, across multiple election cycles, without confusing disclosed contributor geography with the ultimate source of political influence?
verdict.answer_summary: Partially. Within the completed Arkansas federal race-cycle sample, OpenFEC reproducibly supports contributor-state locality shares (itemized), size-bucket structure, candidate totals, and spender-layer independent expenditures across multiple cycles. It does not deliver beneficial-source transparency, and it cannot instrument Arkansas state/local elections at all.
supports_next_design: Define defensible locality measures from contributor-state + size buckets with explicit limitation labels
Inventory Arkansas/state/local disclosure sources (HYP-125 destination universe)
Only then historical measurement across election types
does_not_support: Doctrine or new publication panel from this probe

outside_money_taxonomy.rule: These phenomena are not interchangeable. Do not collapse them into a single 'outside money' claim.

phenomena.name: individual_receipts_outside_constituency
phenomena.definition: Itemized individual contributions to a candidate committee whose disclosed contributor geography is outside the race constituency (state for statewide/Senate; district/state rules for House as locked).
phenomena.probe_evidence: schedule_a/by_state AR vs non-AR shares on principal committees

phenomena.name: pac_committee_money
phenomena.definition: Receipts from other political committees (PACs) reported on candidate totals.
phenomena.probe_evidence: candidates/totals other_political_committee_contributions (stored as pac_contributions in probe)

phenomena.name: party_money
phenomena.definition: Receipts from party committees reported on candidate totals.
phenomena.probe_evidence: OpenFEC candidates/totals political_party_committee_contributions field exists; not separately stored in locality probe v1 — pull on measure-lock enrich

phenomena.name: independent_expenditures
phenomena.definition: Schedule E spending supporting/opposing a candidate by committees other than the candidate's authorized committee.

phenomena.name: organizational_intermediary_funding
phenomena.definition: Funds routed through nonprofits, conduits, joint fundraising, or layered committees before appearing as a contributor or spender.
phenomena.probe_evidence: Visible only when intermediary itself is the disclosed contributor/spender; layers behind often opaque

phenomena.name: untraceable_beneficial_source_funding
phenomena.definition: Material election spending whose significant original human/organizational funders cannot be identified from public disclosure.
phenomena.probe_evidence: Chain break after spender committee on Schedule E; dark-money patterns

four_answers.q1_contributor_geography_reproducibly_me: YES, with limitations — OpenFEC schedule_a/by_state reproducibly yields itemized contributor-state AR vs non-AR shares for principal campaign committees across the completed AR federal sample.
four_answers.q2_locality_comparable_across_cycles_can: YES, for federal principal committees using a locked geography rule (state for Senate; House district vs state rule still needs freeze). Multi-cycle comparison demonstrated 2018–2024 for AR-02/AR-04 and Senate on-cycle years.
four_answers.q4_where_money_trail_becomes_opaque: After the disclosed contributor (Schedule A) or spending committee (Schedule E). Intermediary layers and significant original funders are often NOT OBSERVABLE — especially individual/corp → nonprofit → PAC → super PAC → expenditure.
